items.title: [Bug]: RecoverSSM align mode commits the final SSM state to an unwritten block at exact block boundaries (floor vs ceil-1)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

Reproduced on a downstream fork, not on stock vLLM: Morrowmake/vllm-cmp170hx 1.7.0 (`v0.30.1rc1.dev368+gc1ce6491e`). It routes GLM-5 KDA layers through the Kimi-K3 RecoverSSM kernels. 4× SM80 GPUs (CMP 170HX, 64 GB), TP4, DFlash spec decode, prefix caching on (`mamba_cache_mode=align`), Mamba block size 1152.

Both affected lines are unchanged on `main` @ 0872ddf4b96d.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

In align mode, RecoverSSM puts the final committed state in column `floor(x / B)`. The rest of the align path uses `ceil(x / B) - 1`:

- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:1482`: `prev_state_idx = (num_computed_tokens - 1) // block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/mamba_utils.py:467`: `dest_block_idx = aligned_new_computed // block_size - 1`

The two RecoverSSM sites:

- `vllm/models/kimi_k3/nvidia/ops/recoverssm.py:287` (`_prepare_commit_plan_kernel`): `final_num_computed // mamba_block_size`
- `vllm/v1/worker/gpu/model_states/recoverssm.py:97` (`_postprocess_recoverssm_align_kernel`): `(num_computed + num_sampled) // MAMBA_BLOCK_SIZE`

The two conventions agree except when `x` is an exact multiple of `B`. There they differ, and that happens when a verify step ends exactly on a block boundary with all drafts accepted. RecoverSSM then commits the state to column `k`, while the next step reads its recurrent and conv state from a block this request never wrote. New Mamba blocks are not zeroed (#56524), so the state is garbage, or another request's state.

Observed effect: generation loses context mid-word a few tokens after a multiple of 1152, then repeats a token until `max_tokens` (`…Inputhandlehandlehandle…`, `locklocklock…`).

Found and diagnosed by @YulHeon in Morrowmake/glm53-flash-cmp170hx-recipe#7, which has the boundary-position analysis.

**Proposed fix**: use `ceil - 1` in both places. It does not change anything when `x` is not a multiple of `B`.

items.title: [Bug]: Sparse MLA indexer's expanded_block_table_buffer is allocated after KV sizing (1 GiB at 1M context)
items.bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ 9367d8b969, B200, Model Runner V2, DSA models (sparse MLA indexer).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

The sparse MLA indexer's metadata builder allocates `expanded_block_table_buffer` (`vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`):

```python
self.expanded_block_table_buffer = torch.zeros(
    (scheduler_config.max_num_batched_tokens, block_table_width), dtype=torch.int32, ...
)
```

Builders are constructed during KV cache initialization, after available memory has been profiled and the KV cache sized. So this buffer isn't accounted for and comes out of the activation headroom.

It grows with both `max_num_batched_tokens` and `max_model_len`. With the default 16384 batched tokens and `max_model_len=1048576` (block size 64), it's 16384 × 16384 × 4 B = **1 GiB** per GPU.

On 1×B200 (GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers, `max_model_len=1048576`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.97`), persistent allocations ended up about 1.9 GiB above the planned budget, with or without HiSparse; this buffer is the largest identified piece. A long prefill then OOMed when a 2.25 GiB MoE workspace allocation couldn't fit. The same config without HiSparse failed the same way at 0.975.

Possible fixes: allocate it before memory profiling so it's counted, or size it to what the indexer actually needs. Decode token counts can in principle reach `max_num_batched_tokens`, so shrinking it needs care.

Related: #60429 (same class of bug in HiSparse, a buffer allocated after KV sizing).

### Before submitting a new issue...

- [x] Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the [documentation page](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/), which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.

items.title: [Feature] Add PCP O-Proj tensor parallelism
items.bodyExcerpt:
This PR adds an opt-in `--enable-pcp-o-proj-tp` path that shards the resident MLA O-Proj parameter across the combined PCP-by-TP rank grid while preserving the existing TP reduction semantics.

## Summary

The feature further partitions each TP-local O-Proj input shard across the PCP group, reducing the resident O-Proj parameter on each rank to `1 / PCP` of its standard TP layout. Execution requires `decode_context_parallel_size=1` and eager mode.

Supported architectures are DeepSeek V2, V3, and V3.2, plus GLM-4 MoE Lite and the GLM-5 family MLA architecture. Supported O-Proj representations are `UnquantizedLinearMethod` and ModelOpt W4A4 NVFP4 with a CUTLASS-compatible post-load layout. The NVFP4 adapter is an implementation example for quantized methods; its packed weight and swizzled block scale are handled explicitly. Other post-load layouts fail during post-load processing.

## Runtime behavior

The model runner records the logical, pre-partition batch type and propagates it consistently to every PCP rank. This keeps the collective decision identical even when PCP token partitioning gives different local batch shapes to different ranks.

- For prefill or mixed batches, generic MLA starts an asynchronous O-Proj weight all-gather after Q/KV normalization and before the remaining Q projection, RoPE, indexer, and main attention work. O-Proj waits for the gather only when the full TP shard is needed, then runs the normal TP-local O-Proj computation.
- For decode-only batches, each rank slices the TP attention output to its local PCP feature shard, computes a partial O-Proj result with the resident weight, and all-reduces that result over PCP.
- The existing TP reduction behavior remains unchanged, including paths where TP reduction is handled outside O-Proj.

items.bodyExcerpt:
# [KV Offload] Scope offload group configs to prefix-cacheable KV cache groups

## Purpose

`build_offloading_config` (`vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/offloading/config.py`) builds an `OffloadingGroupConfig` for **every** `kv_cache_group` and then asserts, for all of them:

```
assert group.tokens_per_block % tokens_per_hash == 0, (
    f"tokens_per_block={group.tokens_per_block} not divisible by "
    f"tokens_per_hash={tokens_per_hash}. "
    f"Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need "
    f"--enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes."
)
```

But `tokens_per_hash` comes from `resolve_kv_cache_block_sizes` (`vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`), which derives the hash granularity from **prefix-cacheable groups only** (`hashing_sizes = [... if group.kv_cache_spec.prefix_cacheable]`). The two sides disagree about which groups are in scope, so any hybrid model with a non-prefix-cacheable scratch group (`CircularBufferSpec.prefix_cacheable == False`) whose block size does not divide the cacheable groups' hash granularity crashes at boot the moment the OffloadingConnector is enabled:

```
AssertionError: tokens_per_block=4 not divisible by tokens_per_hash=16. Hybrid models (e.g. Mamba+Attention) need --enable-prefix-caching to align block sizes.
```

Enabling prefix caching does not help — the message's advice cannot be followed, because the scratch group is excluded from hash-size resolution *by design* and its ring capacity is set by compression/lookahead geometry, not by the cache block size.

Where this bites: sparse-MLA hybrids that keep a `CircularBufferSpec` ring of pre-compression keys. We hit it deploying GLM-5.3-Flash (support proposed in #53906) on DGX Spark: per rank the layout is MLA + 4 GDN mamba groups at block size 3584 and an SWA drafter group at 64 (all prefix-cacheable, gcd → `tokens_per_hash = 64`), plus a kpool-tail scratch group at block size 4 → `4 % 64 != 0` → boot crash with any `--kv-transfer-config` offloading setup. ## Purpose

DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.2) currently have **no working sparse-attention backend on
consumer Blackwell** (SM12x: RTX 5090, GB10): the native FlashMLA sparse kernels
(`vllm._flashmla_C`) only build for sm90/sm100, and the sole SM12x option,
`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120`, livelocks under sustained load — GPUs pin at 100 % with zero
output until the NCCL watchdog kills the server. Fixes #51921 (on SM12x).

This makes the `FLASHMLA_SPARSE` backend work on SM12x by binding portable **Triton**
implementations of `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` / `flash_mla_with_kvcache` when the native extension
can't serve the device. The kernels are from #49026 (@marksunner, validated there on
sm_121/GB10) — this PR is that work rebased onto current main as a first-class code path
instead of that PR's runtime monkeypatch, with its model-side diffs dropped (main already has
that content). Supersedes/continues #49026 — happy to hand back or co-drive.

## Scope

This path covers **DeepSeek-geometry sparse MLA** — `qk_rope_head_dim = 64`, i.e. the
512 NoPE + 64 RoPE = **576** head layout: DeepSeek-V3.2/V4.1 and GLM-5.2. The Triton kernels

items.title: [Perf][GLM-5.3-Flash] Shard long-context indexer prefill rows across TP
items.bodyExcerpt:
## TL;DR

**How it works / why it is faster:** Instead of repeating sparse-indexer prefill MQA scoring and top-k on every TP rank, partition independent query rows into cost-balanced contiguous slices. Each rank scores its rows against the full available key history; `all_gatherv` reassembles the final int32 indices. This removes redundant computation in exchange for fixed-width index communication, so savings grow with context length. There is no attention approximation. Decode kernels are unchanged; smaller batches retain the existing path (activation requires at least `16,384 × TP` scheduled prefill query rows).

**Performance, baseline → optimized:** main parent `5893426b88f7` → PR head `16934c6e76e5`; GLM-5.3-Flash on 4× H200, TP4, C1, 256 output tokens, 65,536-token batch budget, legacy runner + explicit FA3 backend. Four fresh-process A/B pairs in ABBA/BAAB order; warmups excluded. Throughput below counts input + output tokens at C1, **not saturated serving throughput**.

| Input context | Server TTFT, seconds (B → O) | TTFT reduction | Total tok/s (B → O) | Throughput increase |
|---|---|---|---|---|

items.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Cap glm5next video sampling knobs
items.bodyExcerpt:
Fixes #55726

## Purpose

`glm_sample_frame_indices` walks `duration * target_fps` candidates and
deduplicates only at the end, so `Glm5NextVideoBackend` sizes that walk from the
requested fps rather than from the clip. On a 2-frame, 1-second source it spends
857 ms and 156 MiB to return 2 indices.

This clamps `target.fps` to `source.original_fps`. No sampling rate above the
source rate can return frames the container does not hold, so the walk becomes
bounded by the frame count while the sampled indices stay identical.

## Why not a fixed ceiling

An earlier revision copied GLMGA's `_MAX_FPS = 30` / `_MAX_FRAMES = 2048`. As
@JaredforReal pointed out, that ceiling has no basis in the GLM-5.3-Flash video
processor: its `processor_config.json` sets only `fps: 2` as the default
interval. A fixed 30 would also halve sampling for a legitimate 60 fps request.

Clamping to the source rate needs no magic number, and it makes the `max_frames`
ceiling unnecessary: with fps bounded, `extract_t` cannot exceed the frame count,
so `max_frames=100_000` keeps returning 10_000 indices exactly as on main.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

`Glm5NextLinearAttention.get_state_dtype()` and `Glm5NextForCausalLM.get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config()` call `MambaStateDtypeCalculator.kda_state_dtype()` without the SSM cache dtype. As a result, the KDA recurrent state is always float32, and `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16` is **silently ignored** for GLM-5.3-Flash. Kimi-K3's KDA already passes it through.

This PR passes `cache_config.mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` in both places. `Glm5NextForConditionalGeneration` delegates to the causal-LM class, so it is fixed too.

Why it matters: with bfloat16 the recurrent state page halves. Mamba align-mode prefix caching sizes the attention block from that page, so at TP2 the block shrinks from 2304 to 1280 tokens. With speculative decoding, each running request holds `2 + num_speculative_tokens` state blocks per group, so on decode instances this state is what bounds concurrency.

## Test Plan

- New test `tests/models/glm5next/test_kda_state_dtype.py`:

- Existing tests: `tests/models/glm5next`.
- End to end: GLM-5.3-Flash, TP2, B300, with `--mamba-ssm-cache-dtype bfloat16`:

  - teacher-forced NLL on long-context prompts is unchanged within run-to-run noise vs the float32 state.

items.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Keep batch x heads out of gridDim.z in the shared FLA recurrent kernels
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

The shared FLA recurrent launchers in `vllm/third_party/flash_linear_attention/ops/` put the batch x value-head product in `gridDim.z`:

```python
grid = (NK, NV, N * HV)
```

CUDA caps `gridDim.y`/`gridDim.z` at 65535, so any decode (or spec-decode) batch with `N * HV > 65535` fails to launch with `Triton Error [CUDA]: invalid argument`. For example, 1024 sequences x 64 local value heads, or 2048 x 32. This affects:

- `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule_fwd`: Qwen3-Next / Qwen3.5 GDN decode, OLMo hybrid GDN
- `fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update`: Qwen GDN decode / spec decode
- `fused_recurrent_kda_fwd` in `ops/kda.py`: reuses the same kernel, used by `bailing_moe_v3`

This PR flattens the grid to `grid = (N * HV * NV, NK)`, so `N * HV` lives in `gridDim.x`, whose limit is 2^31 - 1. The kernels recover `i_nh, i_v = pid // NV, pid % NV`, so the V tile varies fastest. This keeps the original launch order: the V tiles of one (sequence, head) stay adjacent and share that head's q/k/g loads in L2. The packed decode kernel in the same file already guards against this limit with `SPLIT_BATCH_HEAD_GRID`. The kernel bodies are otherwise unchanged.

A first version put `N * HV` in X and the V tiles in Y. That spread the V tiles of a head `N * HV` CTAs apart and made KDA decode up to 1.4x slower at large batches; see the benchmark below.

**Not a duplicate:** #56974 fixes the same class of bug, but only in the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA copy (`vllm/models/glm5next/nvidia/...`). It does not touch these shared files. I found no other open PR that changes the grid of these launchers. #54637 and #51508 touch the same files but not the launch grid.

items.title: [Attention] FlashMLA sparse: stage fp8 mixed-batch q/out in the workspace

## Overview

The FlashMLA sparse `fp8_ds_mla` mixed-batch path now writes the head-padded query and the kernel output into the workspace buffers that `FlashMLASparseImpl` already reserves for `max_num_batched_tokens`, so it no longer allocates them on every call. Related: #59305, #57878. Complements vllm-project/FlashMLA#29, which removes the kernel-internal fp32 split-KV `o_accum` buffer (the other 8 GiB at T=32K). This PR only covers the wrapper side.

## Claims

- On the fp8 mixed-batch path, the padded q (`T x 64 x 576` bf16) and the output (`T x 64 x 512` bf16) are written into the reserved workspace, and the output buffer is passed to the kernel via `out=`. At T=32768 this saves 4.25 GiB per call, measured. The workspace was already reserved, so KV cache capacity does not change.
- Outputs and LSE are bit-identical to the allocating path.
- GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 on 8xH100 (TP8, `max_num_batched_tokens=32768`, `gpu_memory_utilization=0.85`) previously hit a runtime OOM in `flash_mla_with_kvcache` during warmup. With this change it serves the same workload without errors, and GSM8K accuracy matches.

items.title: [Bugfix][Attention] Re-plan DSA indexer decode schedule for DBO's reduced DeepGEMM SM count
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo` and an all2all backend that reserves communication SMs (e.g. DeepEP high-throughput), DSA models (DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5.x) crash in the sparse-attention indexer as soon as a microbatched step contains a decode-branch request:

```
RuntimeError: Assertion error (csrc/apis/attention.hpp:346): _schedule_meta_size == num_sms + 1 and _meta_info_size == 2
```

The indexer builder plans DeepGEMM's paged-MQA-logits schedule for the whole GPU, but DBO lowers DeepGEMM's SM count (`set_num_sms(total - VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS)`) while the microbatches run. This PR re-plans the schedule at the call site when the two counts differ. No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `schedule_meta_size`, `dbo indexer num_sms`, `paged_mqa_logits set_num_sms`: 0 results). Rechecked 2026-10-08 against open PRs: #56476 (DeepSeek-V4.1 per-microbatch index state) also edits `sparse_attn_indexer.py`, in different lines, and does not touch the schedule metadata.

## Claims

- Fixes the DSA indexer decode crash under DBO (Model Runner V1 and V2, CUDA + DeepGEMM).
- The re-planned schedule gives bit-identical indexer logits, so the fix does not change results: with it, GLM-5.3 accuracy under DBO matches DBO with SM partitioning disabled (`VLLM_DBO_COMM_SMS=0`), where this code path never runs.
- Separately, GLM-5.3 accuracy with DBO on is well below DBO off (GSM8K ~0.6 vs 0.93) with or without this change. That is a separate, pre-existing DBO bug in GLM-5.x's shared top-k layers that this crash was hiding, fixed in #60734 (see Validation).
- No cost when the SM count is unchanged (one host-side `get_num_sms()` per indexer layer). Under DBO, one ~9 µs metadata kernel per microbatch per forward, reused by all indexer layers. No host syncs; CUDA-graph safe.
- XPU / ROCm paths unchanged.

items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

With `--enable-dbo`, GLM-5.x (DSA with shared top-k layers, `index_topk_freq > 1`) loses about a third of its GSM8K accuracy: 0.93 with DBO off, 0.61 with DBO on. items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Under DBO, `DeepEPHTPrepareAndFinalize` has DeepEP allocate its dispatch outputs on the DBO comm stream, then reads them on the compute stream; the combine input crosses the other way. The caching allocator is never told about these cross-stream reads, so the other microbatch's next DeepEP call can reuse a block and overwrite it before it is read. With the DeepGEMM FP8 MoE this crashes the engine at startup with an illegal memory access in `ep_scatter`. This PR calls `record_stream` on every tensor that crosses between the two streams.

A GitHub search found no existing issue or PR for this. Related: #46990 added a ROCm-only host sync after HT dispatch/combine under DBO, possibly for the same hazard (see Details). #27666 and #38451 fixed other DBO + DeepEP HT problems.

items.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Decouple DeepEP low-latency dispatch size from max_num_batched_tokens
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

`--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency` crashes at startup whenever `--max-num-batched-tokens` is set above a few hundred. This happens with an ordinary prefill-friendly config such as `--max-num-batched-tokens 4096`. The cause is that the per-rank dispatch capacity of the DeepEP LL buffers is taken directly from `max_num_batched_tokens`. This PR decouples the two: the LL buffers are sized for a fixed number of tokens per rank, and larger forward passes are split into several dispatch rounds that stay in sync across the DP ranks.

Related: #57894 / #57915 (draft). That PR adds a fail-fast error for the same 32 GiB limit, but the config still cannot run. This PR makes the config run.

- A clear `ValueError` is raised when a user-set `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` is too small. Previously this was a bare `AssertionError` deep inside DeepEP.
- No behavior change for the default LL config: when `max_num_batched_tokens` is not set it already defaults to 256, so no chunking happens and the buffer size is unchanged.
- No behavior change for other all2all backends. Chunking only triggers when a rank's batch exceeds `prepare_finalize.max_num_tokens_per_rank()`. Other prepare/finalize implementations report `max_num_batched_tokens` or `None` there, so they never trigger it.

items.title: [Core] Add defer mode for long prefills
items.bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Adds `--long-prefill-token-threshold-defer`, off by default. Instead of capping each long prefill at `long_prefill_token_threshold`, long prefills take turns:
- one long prefill per step;
- it runs after the waiting requests, with the leftover budget, if that is at least the threshold;
- one that sat out its turn runs first the next step.

**Why:** with context parallelism, each step costs a fixed amount, plus an amount for each request in it that grows with its context. On H200 (GLM-5.3, PCP8×DCP8, 8192 tokens per step) that is about 230 ms fixed, plus about 335 ms for a request at 1M context. Splitting the budget pays these costs more often. Under load the adaptive threshold also splits short cached prompts, which cuts throughput just when the queue is longest.
